title: The Nuance of Comparison and Loss
english: To show that I will not endure bonds weakly, from your faith. Phil 2:7 And being found in form as a man. The 'as' is not of likeness but of extension, such as 'God is good to Israel', and 'as I loved your law, Lord, instead of having loved it greatly'. Phil 2:16 Instead of 'those who pay attention to the word of life'. And to Timothy he writes: 'Take care of yourself', instead of 'take care to yourself'. Phil 3:8a If through Christ loss is reckoned, it was not evil; for it was gain. And he said: it was not loss, but according to the arrangement of the better things' superiority it is reckoned loss. Phil 3:8b The refuse is a part of the reed, and the reed and the ear of grain sometimes come from the seed.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG Fragmenta in epistulam ad Philippenses u01-rem-early

title: The Seed and the Harvest
english: Therefore, this refuse is ever most useful for the seed to be produced. For just as from a seed comes a root and a reed and an ear of grain, so too from the faith of Abraham—just as from a seed come those under the law, and the reed of the prophets, and the ear of grain already foretelling Christ in secret (Matt 3:12).

But the harvest of these and the thresher at the first presence of the Savior, who gathers the chaff in his hand and cleanses the threshing floor (Matt 3:12). When, therefore, the reed of the law ceased, it was separated like refuse: circumcision, the keeping of Sabbaths, and the others; but the one of faith is clean.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG Fragmenta in epistulam ad Philippenses u01-rem-mid

title: The Necessity of Law and the Pursuit of the Future
english: The wheat, having been concealed by the prophetic pen, was sent to the storehouses of the common master. Therefore, this name of refuse shows the law to be a dwelling-place; and just as without refuse it would not have been possible to be seed, so also without the law the perfection of grace would not have been established.

Regarding Phil 3:13, forgetting the things behind—not as if they were evil, but he says something like this: I am not occupied with remembering my past struggles, but with being anxious for what I will accomplish in the future.
Regarding Phil 4:2, some say that Euodia was the wife of the jailer, and Syntyche the man.
